Stepper

Steppers display progress through a numbered sequence of logical steps. They guide users through multi-step processes like checkout, form wizards, or setup flows.

Basic Stepper (3 Steps)

A horizontal stepper showing three sequential steps.

  1. 1 Account
  2. 2 Profile
  3. 3 Complete
HTML
<ol class="zak-stepper">
    <li class="zak-stepper-step completed">
        <span class="zak-stepper-dot">
            <span class="zak-step-number">1</span>
        </span>
        <span class="zak-stepper-label">Account</span>
    </li>
    <li class="zak-stepper-step active">
        <span class="zak-stepper-dot">
            <span class="zak-step-number">2</span>
        </span>
        <span class="zak-stepper-label">Profile</span>
    </li>
    <li class="zak-stepper-step">
        <span class="zak-stepper-dot">
            <span class="zak-step-number">3</span>
        </span>
        <span class="zak-stepper-label">Complete</span>
    </li>
</ol>

Stepper with Icons

Use icons inside step indicators instead of numbers.

  1. Date
  2. Security
  3. Confirm

    </span>

Stepper with Labels and Descriptions

Add descriptive text under each step label.

  1. 1 Shipping Choose a shipping method
  2. 2 Payment Enter payment details
  3. 3 Review Confirm your order

<li class="zak-stepper-step active">
    <span class="zak-stepper-dot">
        <span class="zak-step-number">2</span>
    </span>
    <span class="zak-stepper-label">
        Payment
        <span class="zak-step-description">Enter payment details</span>
    </span>
</li>

Vertical Stepper

Steps arranged vertically for forms and settings wizards.

  1. 1 Account Details Enter your account information
  2. 2 Billing Address Add your billing address
  3. 3 Review & Submit Review all information before submitting
HTML
<ol class="zak-stepper zak-stepper-vertical">
    <li class="zak-stepper-step completed">...</li>
    <li class="zak-stepper-step active">...</li>
    <li class="zak-stepper-step">...</li>
</ol>

Stepper with Completion States

Steps support done, active, upcoming, and error states.

  1. 1 Done
  2. 2 Active
  3. 3 Error
  4. 4 Upcoming
HTML
<li class="zak-stepper-step completed">    <!-- Completed -->
<li class="zak-stepper-step active">   <!-- Currently active -->
<li class="zak-stepper-step error">    <!-- Error state -->
<li class="zak-stepper-step">          <!-- Upcoming/inactive -->

CSS Classes

Stepper styles are controlled through these CSS classes.

HTML
/* Stepper Container */
.zak-stepper                     /* Base horizontal stepper */
.zak-stepper-vertical            /* Vertical layout */
.zak-stepper-descriptions        /* Labels with descriptions */

/* Steps */
.zak-stepper-step                 /* Base step item */
.zak-stepper-step.completed       /* Completed state */
.zak-stepper-step.active          /* Current/active state */
.zak-stepper-step.error           /* Error state */

/* Step Parts */
.zak-stepper-dot                  /* Number or icon circle */
.zak-step-number                  /* Number label */
.zak-step-check                   /* Check icon (completed) */
.zak-stepper-label                /* Label text */
.zak-step-description             /* Description under label */

JavaScript

Handle step navigation with JavaScript.

HTML
// Set a specific step as active
function setStep(stepperId, stepIndex) {
    const stepper = document.getElementById(stepperId);
    const steps = stepper.querySelectorAll('.zak-stepper-step');
    steps.forEach((step, i) => {
        step.classList.remove('active', 'completed', 'error');
        if (i < stepIndex) step.classList.add('completed');
        if (i === stepIndex) step.classList.add('active');
    });
}

// Navigate next/prev
function navigateStep(stepperId, direction) {
    const stepper = document.getElementById(stepperId);
    const steps = stepper.querySelectorAll('.zak-stepper-step');
    let current = 0;
    steps.forEach((step, i) => {
        if (step.classList.contains('active')) current = i;
    });
    const next = current + direction;
    if (next >= 0 && next < steps.length) {
        setStep(stepperId, next);
    }
}

Accessibility

Follow these accessibility best practices when using steppers.

  • Use an ordered list <ol> to convey step sequence.
  • Mark the current step with aria-current="step".
  • Provide accessible names for step indicators using aria-label or visible text.
  • For completed steps, use aria-label="Step 1: completed, Account" etc.
  • For clickable steps, use buttons or links with proper focus styles.
  • Update aria-live regions when step content changes dynamically.
  • Ensure step errors are announced with aria-live="assertive".
HTML
<ol class="zak-stepper">
    <li class="zak-stepper-step completed" aria-label="Step 1 of 3: completed, Account">
        <span class="zak-stepper-dot"><span class="zak-step-number">1</span></span>
        <span class="zak-stepper-label">Account</span>
    </li>
    <li class="zak-stepper-step active" aria-current="step" aria-label="Step 2 of 3: current, Profile">
        <span class="zak-stepper-dot"><span class="zak-step-number">2</span></span>
        <span class="zak-stepper-label">Profile</span>
    </li>
</ol>
